title: Mentigo: An Intelligent Agent for Mentoring Students in the Creative Problem Solving Process
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '25)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how large language model (LLM)-based agents can be used not just as task assistants but as mentoring agents to support middle school students during creative problem solving (CPS). The authors argue that CPS is valuable for fostering creativity, engagement, and critical thinking, but is difficult to implement well because students need sustained, personalized, and emotionally supportive guidance, which schools often lack the staff resources to provide. The study therefore asks whether an AI mentor agent can scaffold students through the CPS process more effectively than a simpler baseline system.

The intervention is Mentigo, an interactive AI mentoring system built around a six-stage CPS process: problem discovery, information collection, problem definition, solution ideation, solution evaluation, and solution implementation. The system uses a controller agent to track task stage, infer student state, and select guidance strategies, and a mentor agent to generate empathetic, context-sensitive feedback. Its design is grounded in a dataset constructed from authentic classroom interactions collected during two CPS workshops with 57 middle school students and 12 human mentors. The system was then evaluated through a comparative user study with 12 middle school students using a randomized within-subject design, alongside expert review from five experienced educators.

The study took place with middle school students in China and focused on CPS tasks such as smart home innovation and low-carbon campus design. Participants completed both a Mentigo condition and a baseline condition, with questionnaires, learning reports, interaction logs, screen recordings, and post-task interviews used for evaluation. The paper also included formative interviews with teachers and mentors to derive design goals, emphasizing structured task support, diverse guidance strategies, personalized feedback, deeper cognitive engagement, and emotional support.

The main conclusion is that Mentigo improved student engagement and creative outcomes compared with the baseline system. The authors report that the system promoted deeper reflection, better task alignment, and more personalized support through adaptive feedback and mentoring strategies. They position Mentigo as evidence that AI mentor agents can support CPS learning in middle school settings, while also offering design implications for future educational uses of generative AI.

identified_tools.name: Mentigo
identified_tools.description: An interactive LLM-based mentor agent system for guiding middle school students through a six-stage creative problem solving (CPS) process using structured task management, student-state detection, adaptive strategy selection, personalized feedback, and empathetic interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as an AI mentor for middle school students completing CPS tasks (e.g., smart home and low-carbon campus projects), compared against a simplified baseline agent in a within-subject user study.

findings.finding_summary: In a comparative within-subject experiment with 12 middle school students, the paper reports that Mentigo significantly enhanced student engagement and promoted deeper cognitive processes such as analysis and creativity relative to a baseline system. Qualitative participant feedback indicated that Mentigo’s structured guidance and adaptive feedback improved students’ understanding and application of CPS skills, but no effect sizes or inferential statistics are reported in the provided text.
findings.measure: Student engagement; deeper cognitive processes in CPS including analysis and creativity; perceived understanding and application of CPS skills

findings.finding_summary: The abstract states that Mentigo demonstrated significant improvements in creative outcomes in the comparative experiment. The provided text does not report the exact creative outcome metric, statistical test values, or effect sizes.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical comparative user study with a within-subject design, but the provided text reports only a very small sample (n=12) and does not provide sufficient statistical details or outcome reporting to support a stronger causal evidence tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper claims significant improvements in engagement and creative outcomes, suggesting positive impact, but effect sizes and detailed quantitative results are not reported in the provided text, so magnitude remains unclear.
